behavior_items: The reproducer reaches a floating-point self-comparison of the form `if (r_48 == r_48)`, which is a classic NaN test: for ordinary finite values and infinities the comparison is true, while for NaNs it is false.

With default IEEE-like semantics, a comparison against itself is usually treated as side-effect free, so optimizers often simplify or reason aggressively about it during conditional-expression passes such as `cdce` (conditional dead code elimination).

The key semantic change comes from `-fsignaling-nans`: if the operand may be a signaling NaN, evaluating the floating-point comparison can raise the invalid exception. That means the comparison is no longer a purely harmless predicate; evaluating it may have observable runtime behavior.

The second key change comes from `-fnon-call-exceptions`: GCC must conservatively model certain trapping operations, including FP operations that may raise, as potentially throwing exceptions even though they are not function calls.

When both flags are enabled together at `-O1`, GCC's middle end appears to propagate the 'may throw' property onto the comparison used directly as a `GIMPLE_COND` condition. GCC's verifier rejects this state because a GIMPLE conditional test is required to be non-throwing, producing `error: gimple cond condition cannot throw` during the `cdce` pass.

The failure therefore is not a user-code diagnostic but an internal compiler error triggered by an inconsistent intermediate representation: the optimizer creates or preserves a conditional expression whose evaluation is treated as throwable, violating GIMPLE form invariants.

The report shows the bug is highly configuration-specific: `-O1 -fnon-call-exceptions` alone succeeds, `-O1 -fsignaling-nans` alone succeeds, and the same two flags together without optimization also succeed. That isolates the regression to an optimization-time interaction between signaling-NaN semantics, non-call exception modeling, and the `cdce` transformation.

The exercised code path is likely one where GCC tries to canonicalize, fold, or reason about a floating-point condition that normally looks redundant or tautological-like. Under signaling-NaN rules, however, even apparently simple rewrites must preserve the possibility of an FP exception, so ordinary simplification logic becomes invalid unless the comparison is first lowered into an explicit temporary or guarded representation.

Semantically, the reproducer stresses GCC's need to distinguish value equivalence from evaluation equivalence: `x == x` may be logically true for all non-NaN values, but evaluating it can still be exceptional when `x` is a signaling NaN. The bug indicates this distinction is lost somewhere before or during `cdce`.

From a compiler-correctness perspective, the issue is an IR construction/verification bug rather than merely a missed optimization: GCC should either avoid placing a potentially trapping FP comparison directly in a `GIMPLE_COND`, or transform it into a form whose trapping behavior is represented in a verifier-legal way.

A helper routine to help computing the valid input domain for a builtin function. See C99 7.12.7 for details. In this implementation, we only handle single region domain. The resulting region can be conservative (smaller) than the actual one and rounded to integers. Some of the bounds are documented in the standard, while other limit constants are computed assuming IEEE floating point format (for SF and DF modes). Since IEEE only sets minimum requirements for long double format, different long double formats exist under different implementations (e.g, 64 bit double precision (DF), 80 bit double-extended precision (XF), and 128 bit quad precision (TF) ). For simplicity, in this implementation, the computed bounds for long double assume 64 bit format (DF) except when it is IEEE quad or extended with the same emax, and are therefore sometimes conservative. Another assumption is that single precision float type is always SF mode, and double type is DF mode. This function is quite implementation specific, so it may not be suitable to be part of builtins.cc. This needs to be revisited later to see if it can be leveraged in x87 assembly expansion.

CHANGE_REGION is true when we're being called from cleanup_empty_eh and we intend to change the destination EH region as well; this means EH_LANDING_PAD_NR must already be set on the destination block label. If false, we're being called from generic cfg manipulation code and we should preserve our place within the region tree.
Redirect EH edge E to NEW_BB.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: void redirect_eh_dispatch_edge (geh_dispatch *stmt, edge e, basic_block new_bb)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: This is a subroutine of gimple_redirect_edge_and_branch. Update the labels for redirecting a non-fallthru EH_DISPATCH edge E to NEW_BB. The actual edge update will happen in the caller.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: bool operation_could_trap_helper_p (enum tree_code op, bool fp_operation, bool honor_trapv, bool honor_nans, bool honor_snans, tree divisor, bool *handled)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: Helper function for operation_could_trap_p and stmt_could_throw_p.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: bool operation_could_trap_p (enum tree_code op, bool fp_operation, bool honor_trapv, tree divisor)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: Return true if operation OP may trap. FP_OPERATION is true if OP is applied on floating-point values. HONOR_TRAPV is true if OP is applied on integer type operands that may trap. If OP is a division operator, DIVISOR contains the value of the divisor.
Returns true if it is possible to prove that the index of an array access REF (an ARRAY_REF expression) falls into the array bounds.
Returns true if it is possible to prove that the range of an array access REF (an ARRAY_RANGE_REF expression) falls into the array bounds.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: bool access_in_bounds_of_type_p (tree type, poly_uint64 size, poly_uint64 offset)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: Return true iff a BIT_FIELD_REF <(TYPE)???, SIZE, OFFSET> would access a bit range that is known to be in bounds for TYPE.
Return true if EXPR can trap, as in dereferencing an invalid pointer location or floating point arithmetic. C.f. the rtl version, may_trap_p. This routine expects only GIMPLE lhs or rhs input.
Return non-NULL if there is an integer operation with trapping overflow we can rewrite into non-trapping. Called via walk_tree from rewrite_to_non_trapping_overflow.
Rewrite selected operations into unsigned arithmetics, so that they don't trap on overflow.
If any subexpression of EXPR can trap due to -ftrapv, rewrite it using unsigned arithmetics to avoid traps in it.
Helper for stmt_could_throw_p. Return true if STMT (assumed to be a an assignment or a conditional) may throw.
Return true if statement STMT within FUN could throw an exception.
Return true if STMT in function FUN must be assumed necessary because of non-call exceptions.
Return true if expression T could throw an exception.
Return true if STMT can throw an exception that is not caught within its function FUN. FUN can be NULL but the function is extra conservative then.
Return true if STMT can throw an exception that is caught within its function FUN.
Given a statement STMT in IFUN, if STMT can no longer throw, then remove any entry it might have from the EH table. Return true if any change was made.
Likewise, but always use the current function.

Given a statement OLD_STMT and a new statement NEW_STMT that has replaced OLD_STMT in the function, remove OLD_STMT from the EH table and put NEW_STMT in the table if it should be in there. Return TRUE if a replacement was done that my require an EH edge purge.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: bool maybe_duplicate_eh_stmt_fn (struct function *new_fun, gimple *new_stmt, struct function *old_fun, gimple *old_stmt, hash_map<void *, void *> *map, int default_lp_nr)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: Given a statement OLD_STMT in OLD_FUN and a duplicate statement NEW_STMT in NEW_FUN, copy the EH table data from OLD_STMT to NEW_STMT. The MAP operand is the return value of duplicate_eh_regions.
Similar, but both OLD_STMT and NEW_STMT are within the current function, and thus no remapping is required.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: static bool same_handler_p (gimple_seq oneh, gimple_seq twoh)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: Returns TRUE if oneh and twoh are exception handlers (gimple_try_cleanup of GIMPLE_TRY) that are similar enough to be considered the same. Currently this only handles handlers consisting of a single call, as that's the important case for C++: a destructor call for a particular object showing up in multiple handlers.

Optimize try { A() } finally { try { ~B() } catch { ~A() } } try { ... } finally { ~A() } into try { A() } catch { ~B() } try { ~B() ... } finally { ~A() } This occurs frequently in C++, where A is a local variable and B is a temporary used in the initializer for A.
Perform EH refactoring optimizations that are simpler to do when code flow has been lowered but EH structures haven't.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: static bool lower_resx (basic_block bb, gresx *stmt, hash_map<eh_region, tree> *mnt_map)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: At the end of gimple optimization, we can lower RESX.
Try to optimize var = {v} {CLOBBER} stmts followed just by external throw.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: static int sink_clobbers (basic_block bb, gimple_seq *sunk = NULL, bool *found_opportunity = NULL)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: Try to sink var = {v} {CLOBBER} stmts followed just by internal throw to successor BB. SUNK, if not NULL, is an array of sequences indexed by basic-block index to sink to and to pick up sinking opportunities from. If FOUND_OPPORTUNITY is not NULL then do not perform the optimization but set *FOUND_OPPORTUNITY to true.
At the end of inlining, we can lower EH_DISPATCH. Return true when we have found some duplicate labels and removed some edges.

Walk statements, see what regions and, optionally, landing pads are really referenced. Returns in R_REACHABLEP an sbitmap with bits set for reachable regions, and in LP_REACHABLE an sbitmap with bits set for reachable landing pads. Passing NULL for LP_REACHABLE is valid, in this case only reachable regions are marked. The caller is responsible for freeing the returned sbitmaps.
Remove unreachable handlers and unreachable landing pads.
Remove unreachable handlers if any landing pads have been removed after last ehcleanup pass (due to gimple_purge_dead_eh_edges).

Remove regions that do not have landing pads. This assumes that remove_unreachable_handlers has already been run, and that we've just manipulated the landing pads since then. Preserve regions with landing pads and regions that prevent exceptions from propagating further, even if these regions are not reachable.

Undo critical edge splitting on an EH landing pad. Earlier, we optimisticaly split all sorts of edges, including EH edges. The optimization passes in between may not have needed them; if not, we should undo the split. Recognize this case by having one EH edge incoming to the BB and one normal edge outgoing; BB should be empty apart from the post_landing_pad label. Note that this is slightly different from the empty handler case handled by cleanup_empty_eh, in that the actual handler may yet have actual code but the landing pad has been separated from the handler. As such, cleanup_empty_eh relies on this transformation having been done first.
Examine each landing pad block and see if it matches unsplit_eh.
Wrapper around unsplit_all_eh that makes it usable everywhere.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: static bool cleanup_empty_eh_merge_phis (basic_block new_bb, basic_block old_bb, edge old_bb_out, bool change_region)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: A subroutine of cleanup_empty_eh. Redirect all EH edges incoming to OLD_BB to NEW_BB; return true on success, false on failure. OLD_BB_OUT is the edge into NEW_BB from OLD_BB, so if we miss any PHI variables from OLD_BB we can pick them up from OLD_BB_OUT. Virtual PHIs may be deleted and marked for renaming.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: static void cleanup_empty_eh_move_lp (basic_block bb, edge e_out, eh_landing_pad lp, eh_region new_region)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: A subroutine of cleanup_empty_eh. Move a landing pad LP from its old region to NEW_REGION at BB.

gcc/tree-eh.cc.signature: static bool cleanup_empty_eh_unsplit (basic_block bb, edge e_out, eh_landing_pad lp)
gcc/tree-eh.cc.summary: A subroutine of cleanup_empty_eh. Handle more complex cases of unsplitting than unsplit_eh was prepared to handle, e.g. when multiple incoming edges and phis are involved.
Return true if edge E_FIRST is part of an empty infinite loop or leads to such a loop through a series of single successor empty bbs.

Examine the block associated with LP to determine if it's an empty handler for its EH region. If so, attempt to redirect EH edges to an outer region. Return true the CFG was updated in any way. This is similar to jump forwarding, just across EH edges.
Do a post-order traversal of the EH region tree. Examine each post_landing_pad block and see if we can eliminate it as empty.

Perform cleanups and lowering of exception handling 1) cleanups regions with handlers doing nothing are optimized out 2) MUST_NOT_THROW regions that became dead because of 1) are optimized out 3) Info about regions that are containing instructions, and regions reachable via local EH edges is collected 4) Eh tree is pruned for regions no longer necessary. TODO: Push MUST_NOT_THROW regions to the root of the EH tree. Unify those that have the same failure decl and locus.
Verify that BB containing STMT as the last statement, has precisely the edge that make_eh_edge would create.
Similarly, but handle GIMPLE_EH_DISPATCH specifically.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool can_refer_decl_in_current_unit_p (tree decl, tree from_decl)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Return true when DECL can be referenced from current unit. FROM_DECL (if non-null) specify constructor of variable DECL was taken from. We can get declarations that are not possible to reference for various reasons: 1) When analyzing C++ virtual tables. C++ virtual tables do have known constructors even when they are keyed to other compilation unit. Those tables can contain pointers to methods and vars in other units. Those methods have both STATIC and EXTERNAL set. 2) In WHOPR mode devirtualization might lead to reference to method that was partitioned elsehwere. In this case we have static VAR_DECL or FUNCTION_DECL that has no corresponding callgraph/varpool node declaring the body. 3) COMDAT functions referred by external vtables that we devirtualize only during final compilation stage. At this time we already decided that we will not output the function body and thus we can't reference the symbol directly.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: tree canonicalize_constructor_val (tree cval, tree from_decl)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: CVAL is value taken from DECL_INITIAL of variable. Try to transform it into acceptable form for is_gimple_min_invariant. FROM_DECL (if non-NULL) specify variable whose constructor contains CVAL.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: tree get_symbol_constant_value (tree sym)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: If SYM is a constant variable with known value, return the value. NULL_TREE is returned otherwise.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static tree maybe_fold_reference (tree expr)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Subroutine of fold_stmt. We perform constant folding of the memory reference tree EXPR.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: bool valid_gimple_rhs_p (tree expr)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Return true if EXPR is an acceptable right-hand-side for a GIMPLE assignment. We validate the entire tree, not just the root node, thus catching expressions that embed complex operands that are not permitted in GIMPLE. This function is needed because the folding routines in fold-const.cc may return such expressions in some cases, e.g., an array access with an embedded index addition. It may make more sense to have folding routines that are sensitive to the constraints on GIMPLE operands, rather than abandoning any any attempt to fold if the usual folding turns out to be too aggressive.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static tree fold_gimple_assign (gimple_stmt_iterator *si)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Attempt to fold an assignment statement pointed-to by SI. Returns a replacement rhs for the statement or NULL_TREE if no simplification could be made. It is assumed that the operands have been previously folded.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: void gsi_replace_with_seq_vops (gimple_stmt_iterator *si_p, gimple_seq stmts)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Replace a statement at *SI_P with a sequence of statements in STMTS, adjusting the replacement stmts location and virtual operands. If the statement has a lhs the last stmt in the sequence is expected to assign to that lhs.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static void finish_update_gimple_call (gimple_stmt_iterator *si_p, gimple *new_stmt, gimple *stmt)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Helper function for update_gimple_call and gimplify_and_update_call_from_tree. A GIMPLE_CALL STMT is being replaced with GIMPLE_CALL NEW_STMT.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: bool update_gimple_call (gimple_stmt_iterator *si_p, tree fn, int nargs, ...)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Update a GIMPLE_CALL statement at iterator *SI_P to call to FN with number of arguments NARGS, where the arguments in GIMPLE form follow NARGS argument.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool valid_gimple_call_p (tree expr)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Return true if EXPR is a CALL_EXPR suitable for representation as a single GIMPLE_CALL statement. If the arguments require further gimplification, return false.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: void gimplify_and_update_call_from_tree (gimple_stmt_iterator *si_p, tree expr)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Convert EXPR into a GIMPLE value suitable for substitution on the RHS of an assignment. Insert the necessary statements before iterator *SI_P. The statement at *SI_P, which must be a GIMPLE_CALL is replaced. If the call is expected to produces a result, then it is replaced by an assignment of the new RHS to the result variable. If the result is to be ignored, then the call is replaced by a GIMPLE_NOP. A proper VDEF chain is retained by making the first VUSE and the last VDEF of the whole sequence be the same as the replaced statement and using new SSA names for stores in between.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static void dump_transformation (gcall *from, gcall *to)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Print a message in the dump file recording transformation of FROM to TO.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: void replace_call_with_value (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree val)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Replace the call at *GSI with the gimple value VAL.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static void replace_call_with_call_and_fold (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, gimple *repl)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Replace the call at *GSI with the new call REPL and fold that again.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool var_decl_component_p (tree var)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Return true if VAR is a VAR_DECL or a component thereof.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool size_must_be_zero_p (tree size)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Return TRUE if the SIZE argument, representing the size of an object, is in a range of values of which exactly zero is valid.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_memory_op (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree dest, tree src, enum built_in_function code)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold function call to builtin mem{{,p}cpy,move}. Try to detect and diagnose (otherwise undefined) overlapping copies without preventing folding. When folded, GCC guarantees that overlapping memcpy has the same semantics as memmove. Call to the library memcpy need not provide the same guarantee. Return false if no simplification can be made.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_bcmp (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Transform a call to built-in bcmp(a, b, len) at *GSI into one to built-in memcmp (a, b, len).

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_bcopy (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Transform a call to built-in bcopy (src, dest, len) at *GSI into one to built-in memmove (dest, src, len).

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_bzero (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Transform a call to built-in bzero (dest, len) at *GSI into one to built-in memset (dest, 0, len).

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_memset (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree c, tree len)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold function call to builtin memset or bzero at *GSI setting the memory of size LEN to VAL. Return whether a simplification was made.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool get_range_strlen_tree (tree arg, bitmap visited, strlen_range_kind rkind, c_strlen_data *pdata, unsigned eltsize)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Helper of get_range_strlen for ARG that is not an SSA_NAME.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool get_range_strlen (tree arg, bitmap visited, strlen_range_kind rkind, c_strlen_data *pdata, unsigned eltsize)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: For an ARG referencing one or more strings, try to obtain the range of their lengths, or the size of the largest array ARG referes to if the range of lengths cannot be determined, and store all in *PDATA. For an integer ARG (when RKIND == SRK_INT_VALUE), try to determine the maximum constant value. If ARG is an SSA_NAME, follow its use-def chains. When RKIND == SRK_STRLEN, then if PDATA->MAXLEN is not equal to the determined length or if we are unable to determine the length, return false. VISITED is a bitmap of visited variables. RKIND determines the kind of value or range to obtain (see strlen_range_kind). Set PDATA->DECL if ARG refers to an unterminated constant array. On input, set ELTSIZE to 1 for normal single byte character strings, and either 2 or 4 for wide characer strings (the size of wchar_t). Return true if *PDATA was successfully populated and false otherwise.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: bool get_range_strlen (tree arg, c_strlen_data *pdata, unsigned eltsize)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Try to obtain the range of the lengths of the string(s) referenced by ARG, or the size of the largest array ARG refers to if the range of lengths cannot be determined, and store all in *PDATA which must be zero-initialized on input except PDATA->MAXBOUND may be set to a non-null tree node other than INTEGER_CST to request to have it set to the length of the longest string in a PHI. ELTSIZE is the expected size of the string element in bytes: 1 for char and some power of 2 for wide characters. Return true if the range [PDATA->MINLEN, PDATA->MAXLEN] is suitable for optimization. Returning false means that a nonzero PDATA->MINLEN doesn't reflect the true lower bound of the range when PDATA->MAXLEN is -1 (in that case, the actual range is indeterminate, i.e., [0, PTRDIFF_MAX - 2].

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static tree get_maxval_strlen (tree arg, strlen_range_kind rkind, tree *nonstr = NULL)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Return the maximum value for ARG given RKIND (see strlen_range_kind). For ARG of pointer types, NONSTR indicates if the caller is prepared to handle unterminated strings. For integer ARG and when RKIND == SRK_INT_VALUE, NONSTR must be null. If an unterminated array is discovered and our caller handles unterminated arrays, then bubble up the offending DECL and return the maximum size. Otherwise return NULL.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool known_lower (gimple *stmt, tree len, tree size, bool strict = false)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Return true if LEN is known to be less than or equal to (or if STRICT is true, strictly less than) the lower bound of SIZE at compile time and false otherwise.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_strcpy (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree dest, tree src)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold function call to builtin strcpy with arguments DEST and SRC. If LEN is not NULL, it represents the length of the string to be copied. Return NULL_TREE if no simplification can be made.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_strncpy (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree dest, tree src, tree len)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold function call to builtin strncpy with arguments DEST, SRC, and LEN. If SLEN is not NULL, it represents the length of the source string. Return NULL_TREE if no simplification can be made.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_strchr (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, bool is_strrchr)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold function call to builtin strchr or strrchr. If both arguments are constant, evaluate and fold the result, otherwise simplify str(r)chr (str, 0) into str + strlen (str). In general strlen is significantly faster than strchr due to being a simpler operation.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_strstr (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold function call to builtin strstr. If both arguments are constant, evaluate and fold the result, additionally fold strstr (x, "") into x and strstr (x, "c") into strchr (x, 'c').

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_strcat (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree dst, tree src)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Simplify a call to the strcat builtin. DST and SRC are the arguments to the call. Return NULL_TREE if no simplification was possible, otherwise return the simplified form of the call as a tree. The simplified form may be a constant or other expression which computes the same value, but in a more efficient manner (including calls to other builtin functions). The call may contain arguments which need to be evaluated, but which are not useful to determine the result of the call. In this case we return a chain of COMPOUND_EXPRs. The LHS of each COMPOUND_EXPR will be an argument which must be evaluated. COMPOUND_EXPRs are chained through their RHS. The RHS of the last COMPOUND_EXPR in the chain will contain the tree for the simplified form of the builtin function call.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_strcat_chk (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call to the __strcat_chk builtin FNDECL. DEST, SRC, and SIZE are the arguments to the call.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_strncat (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Simplify a call to the strncat builtin.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_strncat_chk (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call to the __strncat_chk builtin with arguments DEST, SRC, LEN, and SIZE.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static tree gimple_load_first_char (location_t loc, tree str, gimple_seq *stmts)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Build and append gimple statements to STMTS that would load a first character of a memory location identified by STR. LOC is location of the statement.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_string_compare (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call to the str{n}{case}cmp builtin pointed by GSI iterator.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_memchr (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call to the memchr pointed by GSI iterator.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_fputs (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree arg0, tree arg1, bool unlocked)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call to the fputs builtin. ARG0 and ARG1 are the arguments to the call. IGNORE is true if the value returned by the builtin will be ignored. UNLOCKED is true is true if this actually a call to fputs_unlocked. If LEN in non-NULL, it represents the known length of the string. Return NULL_TREE if no simplification was possible.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_memory_chk (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree dest, tree src, tree len, tree size, enum built_in_function fcode)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call to the __mem{cpy,pcpy,move,set}_chk builtin. DEST, SRC, LEN, and SIZE are the arguments to the call. IGNORE is true, if return value can be ignored. FCODE is the BUILT_IN_* code of the builtin. If MAXLEN is not NULL, it is maximum length passed as third argument.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_stxcpy_chk (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree dest, tree src, tree size, enum built_in_function fcode)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call to the __st[rp]cpy_chk builtin. DEST, SRC, and SIZE are the arguments to the call. IGNORE is true if return value can be ignored. FCODE is the BUILT_IN_* code of the builtin. If MAXLEN is not NULL, it is maximum length of strings passed as second argument.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_stxncpy_chk (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree dest, tree src, tree len, tree size, enum built_in_function fcode)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call to the __st{r,p}ncpy_chk builtin. DEST, SRC, LEN, and SIZE are the arguments to the call. If MAXLEN is not NULL, it is maximum length passed as third argument. IGNORE is true if return value can be ignored. FCODE is the BUILT_IN_* code of the builtin.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_stpcpy (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold function call to builtin stpcpy with arguments DEST and SRC. Return NULL_TREE if no simplification can be made.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_snprintf_chk (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, enum built_in_function fcode)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call EXP to {,v}snprintf having NARGS passed as ARGS. Return NULL_TREE if a normal call should be emitted rather than expanding the function inline. FCODE is either BUILT_IN_SNPRINTF_CHK or BUILT_IN_VSNPRINTF_CHK. If MAXLEN is not NULL, it is maximum length passed as second argument.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_sprintf_chk (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, enum built_in_function fcode)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Fold a call EXP to __{,v}sprintf_chk having NARGS passed as ARGS. Return NULL_TREE if a normal call should be emitted rather than expanding the function inline. FCODE is either BUILT_IN_SPRINTF_CHK or BUILT_IN_VSPRINTF_CHK.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: bool gimple_fold_builtin_sprintf (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Simplify a call to the sprintf builtin with arguments DEST, FMT, and ORIG. ORIG may be null if this is a 2-argument call. We don't attempt to simplify calls with more than 3 arguments. Return true if simplification was possible, otherwise false.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: bool gimple_fold_builtin_snprintf (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi)
gcc/gimple-fold.cc.summary: Simplify a call to the snprintf builtin with arguments DEST, DESTSIZE, FMT, and ORIG. ORIG may be null if this is a 3-argument call. We don't attempt to simplify calls with more than 4 arguments. Return true if simplification was possible, otherwise false.

gcc/gimple-fold.cc.signature: static bool gimple_fold_builtin_fprintf (gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, tree fp, tree fmt, tree arg, enum built_in_function fcode)
